data.one_liner: Convert simple HTML and inline CSS styles into RichText or TextSpan widgets.
data.what_it_does: Parses HTML strings with inline CSS and transforms them into Flutter RichText or TextSpan widgets. Supports common text formatting tags like headings, bold, italic, links, and text-related CSS properties such as color, font-size, and font-weight.
use_when: You need to render basic HTML-formatted text with inline styles inside a Flutter app.
You want to handle link clicks embedded inside rich text content.
avoid_when: You need a full web browser view to render complex HTML layouts, JavaScript, or external stylesheets.
You require full support for ordered and unordered lists with custom numbering or symbols.
strengths: Easy to use with simple static methods like HTML.toRichText() and HTML.toTextSpan().
Allows custom global text styling and overriding styles per HTML tag.
Provides a callback mechanism for handling links within the HTML content.
weaknesses: Lists (<ol>, <ul>, <li>) are only partially supported without numbers or symbols.
Input HTML content must be unescaped before passing into version 5.0.0+.
Only handles text-related CSS properties and tags.
data.setup_notes: Requires Flutter version >= 3.22. Input strings must be unescaped prior to parsing.
